newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court tries alleged PKK leaders.
newsitem.headline: German court tries alleged PKK leaders.

text.p: Three alleged leaders of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), banned in Germany as a guerrilla organisation, went on trial on Tuesday charged with a long list of crimes including murder.
Federal prosecutors say the three Kurdish men, aged 28 to 40, were leaders of the PKK and played key roles in a number of criminal acts between 1993 and 1995.
The three led PKK groups in the southern German cities of Nuremberg, Munich and Freiburg until they were arrested in October 1995, prosecutors allege.
The men, who did not enter a plea, are accused of approving plans to murder former PKK members and attacks against property owned by Turks in Germany.
Security at the trial was tight. Dozens of police officers were posted both outside and inside the building, strictly controlling access to the courtroom.
